page: Amazon Web Services r8g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 processors on the arm64 architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, eliminating noisy neighbor issues associated with simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cache architecture features 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of dedicated L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro System, delivers an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, includes hardware AES acceleration, and does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation highlights the memory subsystem as the primary performance strength of the r8g.4xlarge. The PassMark memory test achieves a score of 3,222.48, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Potentially uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 317.2 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 130.27 GB/sec, both placing within the top 25 percent. PassMark database operations demonstrate strong throughput at 23,912.07 operations. Conversely, raw single-core and multi-core computational throughput measured by stress-ng and Geekbench 6 resides in the average category, matching expectations for standard 2.8 GHz clock speeds.

Workload evaluation indicates lower capability for heavy machine learning inference on larger models due to the absence of dedicated accelerators and specialized matrix instruction sets. Text generation on a 70B parameter model is limited to 2.37 tokens per second, falling into the bottom 10 percent. However, for in-memory caching, the instance recorded 35.09 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton4 architecture delivers high memory density per compute core without the overhead of enterprise x86 licensing. Because storage relies entirely on network-attached volumes, storage latency and cost are tied directly to external volume configurations. The r8g.4xlarge is functionally suited for memory-bound applications, including distributed in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-concurrency data ingestion pipelines, and large relational database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 arm64 processors running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 128 GB of memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio without simultaneous multithreading. It features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, no bundled local NVMe storage, and no discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates exceptional memory throughput, placing in the top 10 percent for PassMark memory score and top 25 percent for uncached read and write bandwidth. General CPU metrics, including Geekbench and stress-ng scores, reside within the median tier. The instance exhibits low throughput on larger LLM inference tasks due to the lack of hardware acceleration, but handles memory-intensive throughput efficiently. The r8g.4xlarge is engineered for memory-heavy enterprise workloads including Redis, relational databases, real-time analytics, and caching layers.
